name: Quilt Truck
character: A fabric shop with four wheels: bolts, kits, and a retired delivery van booked to guild nights and county fairs.

sections.eyebrow: The fabric shop that comes to you
sections.title: {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: A retired delivery van fitted with bolts three deep, a notion wall, and a step stool that has seen four counties.

items.title: The bolts
items.body: Three hundred at a time, rotated every run, with the backs and blenders that smaller towns never get.

items.title: The notion wall
items.body: Needles, rulers, and the rotary blades everyone forgot they needed until the wall mentioned it.

items.title: Guild nights
items.body: The truck parks outside your meeting; shopping happens before and after, never during the program.

items.title: Fairs and festivals
items.body: Look for the quilt on the awning and the line of totes.

sections.title: This month's route
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Where the van lands, with hours, parking, and what is fresh on the shelves that week.

sections.heading: Route notes
sections.html: The van runs most Saturdays and guild nights by booking. Winter routes stay south of the pass, and if a stop lands on a harvest or hay day, the route bends around it. Locals know to check the calendar the night before; the van waits for no one but does wait for weather.

sections.title: On the shelves
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: What the van is carrying right now. The stock rotates, so if you see it, buy it.

sections.heading: Holds and special orders
sections.html: Anything on the van can be held until the next stop in your town with a phone call. Bolts by the yard travel; kits are pre-cut and boarded in the cabinet at the back, which is also where the good scrap box lives, priced by the grocery sack.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Two sisters, a retired Step Van the color of marigolds, and a town whose shop closed in 2019.

sections.html:
When the last fabric shop in the county closed, the nearest bolts moved ninety minutes away. The van was a bakery delivery truck, then a false start as a food truck, and finally a shop: shelves bolted where the ovens were, a cutting counter where the sink used to be, and marigold paint chosen because it was on sale in a size that covered a van.

Four years later the route covers six towns and every fair that will have us. The rule painted inside the door is the original one: the fabric goes to the quilters, especially the ones the highway forgot.

items.quote: Our guild night has doubled in attendance since the van started coming. The program chair takes partial credit. The van deserves it.
items.author: A guild secretary

sections.title: Book the truck
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Guild nights, fairs, and festivals within 150 miles. Tell us the date and the parking situation.

items.q: What does a guild night cost?
items.a: Nothing. The truck sells, your guild hosts, and the only ask is twenty feet of curb and a power outlet for the register.

items.q: How much space does the van need?
items.a: Thirty feet to park and open, plus room for a line to form. The awning needs one tree or none.
About 150 miles from base, farther for fairs that book a full weekend. The map on the contact page shows the usual territory.

sections.title: Contact the bus
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Bookings, holds, and the eternal question of whether the van is coming to your side of the mountain.

sections.heading: Home base
sections.when: Saturdays the van is out; weekday mornings by phone
sections.note: The van sleeps in the fairgrounds lot. If the marigold is there, knock on the cab.
